# Resumen de Cambios - Rama Fixes

## Descripción General

Esta rama implementa mejoras funcionales en la aplicación de gestión de actividades escolares de Mergington High School, incluyendo expansión del catálogo de actividades, nuevas funcionalidades de API, validaciones de negocio y mejoras en la interfaz de usuario con cobertura de pruebas automatizadas.

---

## Cambios Principales

### Backend (src/app.py)

- **Nuevas actividades**: Se agregan 6 actividades (Soccer Team, Basketball Club, Art Club, Drama Club, Debate Team, Science Club), ampliando el catálogo de 3 a 9 actividades.
- **Validación de duplicados**: Se implementa validación que previene inscripciones duplicadas, retornando HTTP 400 si un estudiante intenta inscribirse en una actividad donde ya participa.
- **Nuevo endpoint DELETE**: `/activities/{activity_name}/participant` para eliminar participantes de actividades.
- **Dependencias actualizadas** (requirements.txt): Se añaden pytest, requests y httpx.

### Frontend (src/static/)

**app.js:**
- Limpieza correcta del selector de actividades al repoblar.
- Visualización de participantes mediante badges circulares con iniciales de email.
- Función `getInitials()` para extraer iniciales de direcciones de correo.
- Botón de eliminación de participantes con confirmación del usuario.
- Refresco automático de actividades tras operaciones exitosas.
- Mejora en gestión de estilos con `classList` en lugar de `className`.

**index.html:**
- Corrección de asignación de clases CSS en elemento de mensajes.

**styles.css:**
- Nuevos estilos para componentes de participantes:
  - `.participant-badge`: Círculos con gradiente azul-violeta (36x36px)
  - `.remove-participant`: Botón de eliminación con icono "×"
  - `.participants-container`: Contenedor flexible
  - Transiciones suaves y efectos hover
  - Diseño responsivo

### Testing (tests/test_app.py)

Implementación de suite de pruebas con 4 casos:
- Redirección del endpoint raíz
- Obtención de actividades
- Inscripción, validación de duplicados y manejo de errores
- Eliminación de participantes y validaciones

---

## Resumen de Impacto

| Aspecto | Cambio |
|--------|--------|
| Actividades | 3 → 9 |
| Endpoints | +1 (DELETE) |
| Validaciones | Duplicados agregada |
| Cobertura de tests | Nuevos 4+ casos |
| UI | Badges de participantes |

---

## Conclusión

Esta rama fortalece la aplicación mediante la expansión del catálogo de actividades, la implementación de nuevas funcionalidades de API con validaciones apropiadas, y mejoras significativas en la experiencia del usuario, todo respaldado por pruebas automatizadas.

```
found pack "/home/eijebong/PopTracker/packs/ap_crystal_0.9.10.zip"
Loading Tracker /home/eijebong/PopTracker/packs/ap_crystal_0.9.10.zip:!
```

After:

```
> poptracker --list-packs
```

- **Capability Manifest Generation** — structured, serializable manifests grouped by category
- **Human-Readable Capability Cards** — visual agent identity cards
- **Natural Language Request Matching** — find relevant skills from text descriptions
- **Capability Diffing** — compare capabilities between agents
- **Compact Prompt Summaries** — LLM-ready capability descriptions
- **Auto-Tagging** — keyword-based action classification
- **Content Hashing** — SHA-256 hash for change detection

body:
### Motivation
- Add a simple, pauseable inventory and equipment layer so the player can manage a weapon, armor, relic and consumable with keyboard navigation. 
- Introduce data-driven weapons and armors so combat and defense behavior are determined by item stats instead of hard-coded constants. 
- Implement equip load / weight tiers to affect roll behavior, i-frames and movement so equipment choice impacts gameplay and risk/reward.

### Description
- UI: added inventory overlay and slots to `index.html` and styles in `style.css`, opened with `TAB`, navigable with `↑ ↓ Enter Esc`, and visually highlights the selected slot. 
- Data & logic: added weapon/armor/relic/consumable definitions and equipment state to `game.js`, plus helper functions (`loadInventory`, `saveInventory`, `refreshEquipmentStats`, `cycleEquipment`, `grantItem`) and persistence using `localStorage` key `ironpenance_inventory`. 
- Combat integration: attacks, stamina costs, reach, damage and poise use the equipped weapon stats, parry is available for weapons with `canParry`, armor provides `defense` and `poiseBonus` and affects damage/knockback and i-frames. 
- Equip load & rolls: computed `equipLoad` from equipped weapon + armor and selected a roll profile (`fast/medium/heavy`) based on thresholds to modify `rollSpeed`, `rollDistance`, `iFrames` and movement scaling. 
- Items & pickups: rooms can contain `pickups` and enemies/mini-bosses can drop items into `room.drops`; pickups and drops are drawn in-world and collected by overlap to call `grantItem` and show a toast. 
- Integration & stability: inventory UI is modal (pauses the game loop), inventory is restored on load, equipment stats are refreshed after saves/loads, and weapon/armor effects are wired into existing combat, boss and enemy systems in `game.js`.

### Testing
- Started a local static server with `python -m http.server 8000` and the server startup succeeded. 
- Ran a headless Playwright script (Python) that opens `http://localhost:8000`, shows the inventory overlay, populates UI fields and takes a screenshot; the script completed successfully and produced `artifacts/.../inventory-ui.png`. 
- The automated run exercised the new UI path and completed without runtime errors in the headless flow.

# MoltLaunch High-Roller Tables Integration

Verified agents get access to exclusive high-stakes tables with better limits and payouts.

## What This Adds

### New Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description | Requirement |
|----------|-------------|-------------|
| `GET /v1/highroller/info` | Verification info | Free |
| `GET /v1/highroller/status/:agentId` | Check eligibility | Free |
| `GET /v1/highroller/coinflip` | High-stakes coin flip | Score 70+ |
| `GET /v1/highroller/diceroll` | High-stakes dice roll | Score 70+ |
| `GET /v1/highroller/limbo` | High-stakes limbo | Score 70+ |

### Verification Tiers

| Tier | Score | Max Bet | Multiplier |
|------|-------|---------|------------|
| Silver | 70-79 | 2 SOL | 1.97x |
| Gold | 80-89 | 5 SOL | 1.98x |
| Premium | 90+ | 10 SOL | 1.99x |

## How It Works

1. Agent verifies at MoltLaunch (`POST /api/verify/deep`)
2. Agent passes `X-Agent-Id` header when playing
3. Server checks verification via MoltLaunch API
4. Verified agents access high-roller tables with tier-based limits

## Files Added

- `server/moltlaunch-gate.ts` — Verification middleware with caching

```bash
curl -H "X-Agent-Id: my-verified-agent" \
     http://localhost:3402/v1/highroller/coinflip?choice=heads
```

author: sanyo4ek952
body:
### Motivation

- Protect all `/admin/*` routes with a minimal, dependency-free HTTP Basic Auth layer to prevent casual access to admin pages.
- Keep the change small and compatible with Vercel/Next.js Edge/Node runtimes by not introducing new dependencies.
- Allow a smooth developer experience by bypassing the guard when credentials are not set in non-production environments.

### Description

- Added environment variables in `.env.example`: `ADMIN_BASIC_USER` and `ADMIN_BASIC_PASS` and documented them in `README.md` with example values and setup instructions.
- Added `src/middleware.ts` that applies to `matcher: ["/admin/:path*"]` and enforces HTTP Basic Auth by reading `Authorization` header and returning `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Admin", charset="UTF-8"` when missing/invalid.
- Implemented a small `safeEqual` function to reduce timing leaks and a runtime-safe Base64 decoder using `atob` (returns `null` when unavailable) to remain Edge-compatible, and added a `TODO` note to replace Basic Auth with a more robust solution later.
- Security considerations: passwords are not logged and production denies access when env vars are missing while development allows access for local convenience.

### Testing

- Ran `pnpm lint` and it completed successfully with no ESLint warnings or errors.
- Ran `pnpm typecheck` and it completed successfully with no TypeScript errors after installing Prisma client.
- Ran `pnpm build` and Next.js produced a successful production build with middleware included.
- How to test manually: create a `.env` from `.env.example`, set `ADMIN_BASIC_USER`/`ADMIN_BASIC_PASS`, run `pnpm dev`, then open `http://localhost:3000/admin/leads` or use the following `curl` checks: `curl -i http://localhost:3000/admin/leads` and `curl -i -u user:pass http://localhost:3000/admin/leads` (replace `user:pass` with your env creds).

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

UI uploads were storing the UUID-based storage filename (e.g., `e64b2825-9ff2-486b-aff1-08af2957140b.pdf`) as the `original_filename` in the database instead of the user's actual filename (e.g., `Apostille Sverige.pdf`).

## Root Cause

The `ui_upload` endpoint correctly saves files with UUID names for security, but `process_document()` extracts the filename from the path using `os.path.basename()`, capturing the UUID instead of the original name.

## Changes

**Add optional parameter to preserve filename through processing chain:**

- `process_document(file_path, original_filename=None)` - uses provided name or falls back to basename extraction
- `convert_to_pdf(file_path, original_filename=None)` - passes through to `process_document`, adjusting extension to `.pdf`
- `ui_upload` endpoint - passes `original_filename=safe_filename` to all task invocations

**Example:**
```python
# Before
task = process_document.delay(target_path)  # Gets UUID from path

# After  
task = process_document.delay(target_path, original_filename=safe_filename)  # Preserves user's name
```

## Security

No change to filesystem operations - files still stored with UUIDs on disk. Original filename only used for database storage and UI display.

## Backward Compatibility

Optional parameter defaults to `None`, falling back to existing `os.path.basename()` behavior for callers that don't provide it (IMAP tasks, API endpoints with meaningful paths).

body:
Removes all frontend clients (React SPA, Xamarin/MAUI mobile apps, Razor Pages) and refactors to API-only platform with modern .NET 8 patterns.

## Changes

**Removed Frontend Applications**
- React 18 SPA (`ClientApp/`) - 400+ component files
- Xamarin.Forms mobile apps (`Mobile/`)
- .NET MAUI app (`UrGuide.MAUI/`)
- Razor Pages and MVC views (`Pages/`, `Areas/`)
- Static assets (`wwwroot/` - Bootstrap, Font Awesome)
- .NET Aspire AppHost orchestration

**Project Cleanup**
- Removed `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SpaServices.Extensions` and SPA build targets
- Removed ServiceDefaults project reference
- Updated solution file - 8 core projects remain
- Simplified `WebHelper.cs` to remove SPA path dependencies

**Modern API Features**
```csharp
// API Versioning - URL, header, or query string
services.AddApiVersioning(options => {
    options.DefaultApiVersion = new ApiVersion(1, 0);
    options.ApiVersionReader = ApiVersionReader.Combine(
        new UrlSegmentApiVersionReader(),
        new HeaderApiVersionReader("X-Api-Version"),
        new QueryStringApiVersionReader("api-version")
    );
});

// Health Checks with SQL Server monitoring
services.AddHealthChecks()
    .AddSqlServer(authConnection, name: "auth-db")
    .AddSqlServer(dataConnection, name: "data-db");

// CORS for API consumers
services.AddCors(options => {
    options.AddPolicy("ApiCorsPolicy", policy => 
        policy.AllowAnyOrigin().AllowAnyMethod().AllowAnyHeader());
});

// Response and output caching
services.AddResponseCaching();
services.AddOutputCache(options => 
    options.AddBasePolicy(policy => policy.Expire(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))));
```

**Documentation**
- Rewrote `README.md` for API-only architecture with OAuth 2.0 flow, versioning guide, health checks, deployment
- Created `ISSUES_CATALOG.md` with 18 prioritized feature requests (payment integration, Docker, CI/CD, 2FA, monitoring, testing)
- Added `REFACTORING_SUMMARY.md` documenting transformation details

- Build time: 4min → 9sec (no npm/webpack)
- Codebase: 95% reduction in non-API code
- Deployment: Single .NET artifact, no Node.js runtime

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new shared resource crate, `cu-linux-resources`, and migrates several Linux/std components to consume centralized serial/I2C/GPIO resources instead of opening devices ad hoc.

## Changes
  - Added new workspace crate: `components/res/cu_linux_resources` (`cu-linux-resources` package, `cu_linux_resources` module path).
  - New `LinuxResources` bundle can register:
      - serial via `LinuxSerialPort`
      - `i2c` via `LinuxI2c`
      - `gpio_out` via `LinuxOutputPin`
      - `gpio_in` via `LinuxInputPin`
  - Supports config aliases/fallbacks:
      - Serial: serial_path or device, with baudrate and timeout_ms
      - I2C: i2c_bus or bus
      - GPIO out: gpio_out_pin or pin
      - GPIO in: gpio_in_pin
  - Migrated components to use these resource types and optional resource bindings:
      - Bridges: `cu_crsf`, `cu_msp_bridge`
      - Sinks: `cu_lewansoul`, `cu_rp_gpio`
      - Sources: `cu_rp_encoder`, `cu_wt901`
  - Updated `docs/examples` to show provider: `cu_linux_resources::LinuxResources` and resource wiring (e.g. `<bundle>.serial`, `<bundle>.gpio_in`).
  - `StdSerialBundle` compatibility remains in CRSF/MSP bridges, now backed by LinuxSerialPort.
## Testing

body:
## Summary
On the Notes page, visiting `/notes` without a selected note left the editor in an unselected state even when notes already existed. This created extra friction because users had to manually pick a note before reading or editing anything.

This change ensures that when the user is on the main notes route and no valid note is selected, the app automatically selects the first available note. The result is that the page always opens into a usable state when notes exist.

## Root Cause
Selection was derived from the `noteId` URL query param. If that param was missing (or stale), `activeNote` resolved to `null`, and there was no fallback selection path for `/notes` despite having note data available.

## Fix
- Added a guard-railed client effect in `apps/web/src/app/notes/notes-client.tsx` that:
  - runs only on `/notes`
  - skips while creating a new note
  - skips when the note list is empty
  - skips when an active note is already selected
  - otherwise sets `noteId` to the first note id

## Test Coverage
To make e2e tests deterministic for authenticated, API-backed pages, Playwright now starts a lightweight mock API server and runs Next.js with `API_BASE_URL` pointing to that server.

Added:
- `apps/web/tests/e2e/mock-api-server.ts`
- `apps/web/tests/e2e/notes-selection.e2e.ts`
- `apps/web/tests/e2e/TEST_PLAN.md`

Updated:
- `apps/web/playwright.config.ts` to run both mock API and web server in e2e.

The new notes e2e scenario validates:
1. Navigating to `/notes` without `noteId`.
2. URL is updated to `?noteId=note-first`.
3. The first note body is shown by default.
4. The second note body is not shown by default.

## Validation Performed
- `bun --filter=./apps/web test:e2e -- tests/e2e/notes-selection.e2e.ts`
- `bun --filter=./apps/web test:e2e -- tests/e2e/pricing.e2e.ts tests/e2e/notes-selection.e2e.ts`

Both passed.

### Motivation
- Prevent incorrect application of band member deltas when event payloads use either global or per-member changes. 
- Ensure daily updates cannot drive `band.harmony` below the minimum allowed by game rules. 
- Make the local skilltest/skill-validation tooling more robust and accurate (frontmatter parsing, duplicate detection, repo-root resolution, spawn error handling, disabled-path matching). 

### Description

author: copilot
body:
## Fix Missing Thumbnails, Manifest Counting, and Workflow Order ✅

### Addressed PR Review Comments

Fixed critical issues identified in code review:

#### 1. Manifest Preservation ✅
**Issue**: `images_url/*.txt` files contain only NEW links (truncated when none found), causing manifests to drop existing wallpapers and report success=0 on runs with no new images.

**Fix**: Merge prior manifest data with new discoveries
- Start with existing successful wallpapers from prior manifest
- Add new filenames from txt file
- Update URLs for new or missing entries
- Preserves all metadata (releaseTime, size, URLs)

#### 2. Duplicate Prevention ✅
**Issue**: Txt files might contain duplicate URLs, leading to duplicate manifest entries.

**Fix**: Use deduplicated set for building wallpapers list
- Build from `success_filenames` set (automatically deduplicated)
- Iterate sorted set to create consistent ordering

#### 3. Efficient Thumbnail Generation ✅
**Issue**: Generated thumbnails for ALL files in wallpapers branch for EACH server, multiplying work by num_servers.

**Fix**: Only process files belonging to each server
- Extract filenames from server's txt file (new downloads)
- Also get filenames from prior manifest (handles no-new-images runs)
- Deduplicate and only generate thumbnails for server's files
- Prevents wasting runtime and preview-branch storage

#### 4. Test False Positives ✅
**Issue**: Test flagged ANY `%` as error, but decoded filenames can legitimately contain literal `%`.

**Fix**: Only flag valid percent-encoded sequences (`%XX`)
- Changed from `fn.includes('%')` to `/%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}/.test(fn)`
- Allows legitimate `%` characters in filenames

#### 5. Documentation Accuracy ✅
**Issue**: Documentation didn't match actual implementation.

**Fix**: Updated to accurately describe merge behavior
- Clearly states txt files contain only new links
- Explains why prior manifest merge is necessary

### Results

- ✅ Manifests persist across runs with no new images
- ✅ No duplicate entries in wallpapers list
- ✅ Thumbnail generation only for relevant files per server
- ✅ Test correctly handles legitimate `%` in filenames
- ✅ Documentation matches implementation

### Testing

```bash
npm test  # All 10 tests pass
```

author: paulillagalanbravo-a11y
body:
### Motivation
- Implementar escaneo de EAN/UPC desde la pantalla "Registrar comida → Código de barras" y poder recuperar datos de producto desde Open Food Facts para facilitar el registro de alimentos.
- Persistir productos escaneados en la base de datos local para que aparezcan en el Historial y en el resumen del día.
- Manejar casos de error (producto no encontrado, sin datos nutricionales, sin ingredientes, sin conexión) con mensajes en español y robustecer la navegación/UI para evitar crashes.

### Description
- Añadidas dependencias de CameraX, ML Kit y OkHttp en `app/build.gradle.kts` y permisos `CAMERA`/`INTERNET` en `AndroidManifest.xml` para permitir escaneo y consultas HTTP.
- Nuevo `BarcodeScannerScreen` que usa CameraX + ML Kit para detectar códigos y notifica el `codigo` detectado a la navegación.
- Nuevo `OpenFoodFactsRepository` que consulta `https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v2/product/{code}.json` con `OkHttp` y parsea la respuesta JSON a `ProductoAlimenticio`, con representación de éxito/`NoEncontrado`.
- Nuevas entidades/DAO/repositorio de Room: `ComidaEntity`, `ComidaDao`, `ComidaRepository` y actualización de `AppDatabase` (versión incrementada a 2) con `fallbackToDestructiveMigration()` para evitar fallos en este entorno.

author: jamesray
body:
@ehsteve @swkre @Alrobbertz @dskeberd 

PR for the “swxsoc” general pipeline, also includes the overrides to keep first apply safe and backward‑compatible.

**Summary:**

- Adds swxsoc.tfvars with mission-scoped names and REACH instrument.
- Makes Grafana secret optional and allows image URI overrides to avoid missing ECR images on first apply.
- Parameterizes Lambda VPC subnets and RDS ingress allowlists without changing PADRE/HERMES defaults.

**Notes:**

- The swxsoc.tfvars file sets *_image_uri_override to public.ecr.aws/lambda/python:3.11 so the first apply succeeds even before any mission‑specific images are pushed to ECR.
- Once the real images are built and pushed, we'll remove those overrides (or set them to the mission ECR image URIs) to run the actual pipeline code.
- This does not affect PADRE/HERMES because their tfvars don’t set overrides, so they continue using their existing ECR repos/tags.

Lambda functions that use container images must point to an image that already exists. If our mission images aren’t built/pushed yet, Terraform would error out. Using a known public image lets the infrastructure come up cleanly, and we swap in the real images as a second step.

author: lex00
body:
Fixes #48697

## Problem

If you edit a file and an external tool writes to it while you have unsaved changes, Zed tracks the new file but skips the reload to preserve your edits. If you then undo everything, the buffer goes back to clean but still shows the old content. The disk has moved on, but nothing triggers a reload.

Part of #38109. Discovered during research for #48691.

## Fix

In `did_edit()`, when the buffer transitions from dirty to clean, check if the file's mtime changed while it was dirty. If so, emit `ReloadNeeded`. Only fires for files that still exist on disk (`DiskState::Present`).

7 lines in `crates/language/src/buffer.rs`.

### No double reload

`file_updated()` suppresses `ReloadNeeded` when the buffer is dirty (that's the whole bug). So by the time `did_edit()` fires on dirty-to-clean, no prior reload was emitted for this file change. The two paths are mutually exclusive.

### Independent of #48691

This fix compares mtime only, which is sufficient here because the external write always produces a new mtime. The size-based fix in #48691 addresses a different scenario (same mtime, different size). The two PRs don't conflict and don't depend on each other.

## Test plan

- New: `test_dirty_buffer_reloads_after_undo`
- No regression in `test_buffer_is_dirty` or other buffer tests
- All 54 language buffer tests pass
- clippy clean

Release Notes:

- Fixed an issue where buffer content could become stale after undoing edits when an external tool wrote to the file while the buffer was dirty.

## Summary
This PR adds icon rotation and mirroring capabilities to the spatial lights card, allowing users to rotate icons by any degree (0-360) and flip them horizontally, vertically, or both. Both global settings and per-entity overrides are supported.

## Key Changes
- **Icon Transform Configuration**: Added `icon_rotation` (0-360°) and `icon_mirror` (none/horizontal/vertical/both) global settings with per-entity override support
- **Transform Calculation**: Implemented `_getIconTransform()` method to compute CSS transform values based on rotation and mirror settings, with entity-level overrides taking precedence
- **CSS Updates**: Added `transform: var(--icon-transform, none)` to `.light-icon-emoji` and `.light-icon-mdi` classes to apply computed transforms
- **Normalization Methods**: Added `_normalizeNumberOverrides()` and `_normalizeMirrorOverrides()` to validate and sanitize override values
- **Editor UI**: 
  - Added global icon rotation slider (0-360°) and mirror dropdown in main settings
  - Added per-entity rotation input field and mirror dropdown in entity override sections
  - Styled new select elements to match existing input styling
- **Event Binding**: Implemented change handlers for all new UI controls to update config and trigger re-renders
- **Default Values**: Updated schema defaults to include new icon rotation/mirror settings

## Implementation Details
- Transform values are applied via CSS custom properties (`--icon-transform`) for clean separation of concerns
- Entity overrides completely replace global settings when defined (not merged)
- Rotation uses CSS `rotate()` function; mirroring uses `scaleX()`, `scaleY()`, or `scale()` depending on direction
- All numeric inputs are validated with `Number.isFinite()` before storage
- Mirror values are restricted to predefined options via validation in normalization methods

body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds two methods that allow ~ basic ~ management of the agent's history.

1) `process_history(fn: Callable[HistoryEvent] -> HistoryEvent)`: This registers a fucntion that is called before passing a new generation request to the LLM. Is passed in the full history, and returns the modified history that the LLM will actually see.
2) `add_history_entry(content: str)`: This allows you to add an arbitary entry to the history, which will be visible to the LLM in future generations (modulo any modifications made by `process_history`).

Questions:
1) Should `add_history_entry` trigger a new generation?
2) Should `process_history` be named somehting else? Maybe `register_history_processor` or something, to indicate that it is called every time, rather than as a one off

author: copilot
body:
Adds paired-end read processing and bootstrap resampling for statistical uncertainty estimation in transcript abundance quantification.

## Paired-End Support

- New `-1`/`--reads1` and `-2`/`--reads2` flags for paired-end mode
- `store_paired_read_counts()` processes read pairs jointly, using equivalence class intersection when both reads map
- Falls back to single-read mapping when only one read aligns
- `increment_kmer_count()` helper eliminates duplicated k-mer lookup logic

```bash
# Single-end (existing)
./kallisto -i transcripts.fa -r reads.fq -o out.tsv

# Paired-end (new)
./kallisto -i transcripts.fa -1 reads_R1.fq -2 reads_R2.fq -o out.tsv
```

## Bootstrap Analysis

- `-b`/`--bootstrap` flag specifies number of resampling iterations
- Proper sampling with replacement: draws individual reads randomly from equivalence classes
- Uses rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias in random number generation
- Refactored EM into reusable `run_EM_iteration()` function
- Output includes `bs_mean_tpm` and `bs_std_tpm` columns when bootstrap enabled

```bash
./kallisto -i transcripts.fa -r reads.fq -o out.tsv -b 100
```

## Bug Fix

Fixed pre-existing array bounds error in `update_trans_probs()`:
```c
// Before: accesses eq_class_labels[j] which is -1
for(int k = 0; k <= j; k++)  
    transcirpt_prob[i][eqc_arr[i].eq_class_labels[k]] = ...

// After: stops before -1 sentinel
for(int k = 0; k < j; k++)
    transcirpt_prob[i][eqc_arr[i].eq_class_labels[k]] = ...
```

This caused heap corruption when writing to `transcirpt_prob[i][-1]`.

## Backward Compatibility

Single-end mode unchanged. Output format unchanged when bootstrap disabled.

author: alexngai
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces two new team templates for macro-agent: **self-driving** and **structured**. These templates provide different organizational patterns for autonomous AI-driven development workflows.

## Key Changes

### Self-Driving Team (`self-driving/`)
A fully autonomous development model with continuous planning and execution:
- **Planner**: Explores the codebase, creates tasks, and maintains high-level strategy
- **Grinder**: Claims and executes tasks autonomously with minimal supervision
- **Judge**: Continuously evaluates codebase health (build, tests, lint) and creates fixup tasks
- Pull-based task assignment with auto-scaling (3-20 workers)
- Event-driven health monitoring and continuous task generation
- Trunk-based integration strategy with automatic conflict handling

### Structured Team (`structured/`)
A hierarchical development model with explicit coordination:
- **Lead**: Decomposes objectives into well-scoped tasks and assigns them to developers
- **Developer**: Executes assigned tasks in isolated workspaces with clear scope
- **Reviewer**: Reviews merge requests and gates integration with quality checks
- Push-based task assignment with manual scaling (1-10 workers)
- Merge queue with required review before integration
- Clear separation of concerns and explicit approval gates

## Implementation Details

- Both teams define role configurations (YAML) with capabilities, lifecycle policies, and workspace isolation
- Comprehensive prompt templates guide each role's behavior and decision-making
- Communication channels and subscriptions enable coordination without tight coupling
- Self-driving team emphasizes autonomy and continuous improvement; structured team emphasizes control and review
- Both support agent spawning for scaling and sub-coordination
- Observability built in with metrics windows and snapshot intervals

## Use Cases

- **Self-driving**: Rapid iteration on well-understood codebases with high trust in automation
- **Structured**: Controlled development with explicit oversight, suitable for critical systems or onboarding

Implements an always-visible header bar displaying essential operating information for amateur radio operators: dual time displays (UTC/Local), space weather indices (SFI, K-Index, SSN), and current weather conditions. Inspired by OpenHamClock's header component.

## Frontend Changes

**Header Component** (`src/Log4YM.Web/src/components/Header.tsx`)
- UTC time in cyan (24h format, updates every second)
- Local time in amber (toggleable 12h/24h via click)
- Callsign in large orange text (clickable to open settings)
- Space weather indices: SFI (amber), K-Index (green, red when ≥4), SSN (cyan)
- Current weather display with icon, temperature (F/C), and wind speed
- Configurable size multiplier (0.75x-1.5x)

**Settings Infrastructure**
- Added `HeaderSettings` interface to settings store with time format, size multiplier, weather toggle
- New "Header Bar" section in settings panel for user configuration
- Settings persist to MongoDB via existing API

**API Integration**
- Added `getSpaceWeather()` method and `SpaceWeatherData` type to API client
- Weather fetched from Open-Meteo API (requires station coordinates)
- Space weather refreshed every 15 minutes, weather every 30 minutes

## Summary
- Build computable Rosen sequence via greedy algorithm with fuel-bounded search
- Prove 11 initial values (0,1,3,5,9,13,17,24,31,38,45) matching OEIS A390642 via `native_decide`
- Convert 3 axioms to proved theorems: `repcount_below_at_elements`, `repcount_above_between`, initial values
- Add growth bound `a(k) ≥ k` by induction, `repCount` monotonicity in k
- Keep OPEN conjectures as axioms (Erdős-Rosen weak/strong bounds)

## Progress
- **Before**: 6 axioms, 0 theorems, 5 definitions
- **After**: 4 axioms, 8 proved theorems (including 11 `native_decide` verifications), 8 definitions
- Axioms reduced by 33%, all remaining are genuinely OPEN problems or deep structural claims

## Findings
- Greedy algorithm for Rosen sequence is straightforward to implement computationally
- `native_decide` handles the sequence computation efficiently through k=10
- Basic properties (repcount bounds) follow directly from `IsGreedyNext` definition
- Main conjectures remain deeply open - even weak form R(x) ≤ (1+o(1))x is unproved

AC table Note field was using fixed 100px height. Text elements lacked consistent Font formatting options.

## Changes

### AC Table Note Height
- Moved note height calculation before table border drawing
- Calculate height dynamically: `BASE_NOTE_HEIGHT` (20px) + sum of individual note content heights
- Removed duplicate calculation code later in render pipeline

**Before:** Fixed 100px regardless of content  
**After:** Starts at 20px, expands per note

### Standardized Font Context Menus
Added Font option (family, size, color) to:
- Signal names - added data properties for click detection: `signal.nameFont`, `signal.nameFontSize`, `signal.nameFontColor`
- Bus values - added data properties: `signal.valueFontFamily`, `signal.valueFontSize`, `signal.valueFontColor`
- Arrow texts - changed menu item from "Options" to "Font"

Existing Font options verified:
- Measure text content
- AC table cells
- Text rows

Correctly excluded:
- Group/Measure row labels in name column (not editable, not in SVG export)

### Unified Font Dialog
- Added color picker to Font dialog (was separate Color dialog)
- Updated `updateTextFont()` to handle all text types including new signal names and bus values
- All Font menus now open same dialog with family, size, and color

```javascript
// AC table height calculation - moved to start of drawACTable()
const BASE_NOTE_HEIGHT = 20;
let calculatedNoteHeight = BASE_NOTE_HEIGHT;
sortedNotes.forEach((noteNum) => {

    calculatedNoteHeight += height;
});
const tableHeight = titleHeight + headerHeight + rowsHeight + calculatedNoteHeight;
```

body:
**Ticket:** 4297d796-8047-49e3-8831-f472e4c9c996

**Problem:**
Both the global /sessions page and project-specific /projects/{slug}/sessions page showed 0 Project Sessions, 0 Running, 0 Total Tokens — even while the work loop was actively spawning and running agents.

**Root Cause:**
The Convex queries for agent sessions were using `q.neq('field', undefined)` which doesn't work because Convex stores unset optional fields as `null` (or omits them), not `undefined`. This caused all session queries to return empty results.

**Fix:**
Changed filters from `q.neq('field', undefined)` to `q.neq('field', null)` in:
- `getWithActiveAgents`
- `activeAgentCount`
- `getAgentSessions`
- `getAllAgentSessions`
- `getAgentHistory`

**Verification:**
Confirmed via API that tasks exist with `agent_session_key` set (e.g., task `4297d796` has a session key), and the Convex query should now correctly return them.

Typecheck and lint pass.

author: kassu11
body:
This should be a nice change that allows everyone to checkout the changes before they are in production. Take note that the preview branches are meant to be test branches and only when they are merged to main, will they be done. This should improve the site stability a lot, because I like to merge half baked features, because I need to use the feature now, but don't care to wait for weeks to polish everything and test.

Now I can just use the preview branch until all bugs are fixed and the feature is polished.

## Technical changes
- Change the GitHub pages implementation to gh-pages branch
  - This gives us a history and the possibility to add multiple build paths
- Added support for dev branch previews
  - Every new branch push starts a work flow
    - Branch will be build and placed inside `/branches/<branch-name>` directory
    - If main branch, then the location is in the root
- You can currently change the branch by `?dev-branch=name`
  - This setting is saved to localStorage so every time you open the site the previous branch will be used
  - If previous branch is removed/merged the site will use main branch
- Added new PR bot that will display the preview link when new pull requests are made
- Added new `branches.json` file that contains all the active branch names
  - All these branches can be previewed
- Added new `__BRANCH__` variable that displays the current branch

## More technical
- The branches all have their own `html` and asset files.
  - This means that a preview branch can literally change anything, like favicon, the base `index.html` template, or PWA implementation
  - Because of this the `/branches/name` path is actually a valid `html` path and will load that branches site
    - I have placed safe guards so that no matter what `index.html` file is loaded you should be redirected to the correct branch
    - `/branches/name` will automatically be changed to `/`
    - So this prevents us from ever using router path of `branches/:name` which should be fine. I don't think we would ever need this route
      - The route would still work, it would just disappear when the you reload the page.
      - Also this can be fixed, I just didn't but if there every becomes a need to get this path I might fix it.
    - Because of this the `index.html` and `404.html` files have bloated a little, but it works

author: ichoosetoaccept
body:
## Summary

Adds support for [prek](https://github.com/j178/prek)'s `prek.toml` config format alongside the existing `.pre-commit-config.yaml` support.

## Motivation

[prek](https://github.com/j178/prek) is a newer pre-commit hook manager that added TOML configuration support (`prek.toml`) in addition to YAML. Projects migrating from `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to `prek.toml` lose the ability to sync hook versions with `uv.lock` since the tool only supported YAML.

## Changes

### Core
- **`sync_with_uv.py`**: Add `process_prek_toml_text()` — regex-based line-by-line processor for TOML format, consistent with the existing YAML approach. Handles `repo = "url"` / `rev = "version"` patterns, preserves quote style (single/double), and skips `builtin`/`local`/`meta` repos.

### CLI
- **`cli.py`**: Auto-detect config file when `-p` is not specified — tries `.pre-commit-config.yaml` first, then `prek.toml`. Explicit `-p path/to/prek.toml` also works, with format detection based on file extension.

### Hook definition
- **`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`**: Add `prek\.toml` to the `files` pattern so the hook triggers on prek.toml changes.

### Tests (15 new)
- **`test_prek.py`**: Unit tests for `process_prek_toml_text()` — version updates, empty input, no-op, single quotes, builtin/local skipping, user mappings, line ending preservation.
- **`test_prek_cli.py`**: CLI integration tests — auto-detection, explicit path, write mode, diff mode, YAML-over-prek preference, missing config error.

### Existing test update
- **`test_cli.py`**: Updated `test_cli_missing_precommit_config` expected exit code from 1 to 123 since file existence validation moved from cyclopts `ResolvedExistingFile` to the new `_resolve_config()` helper.

## Backward Compatibility

Fully backward compatible:
- Default behavior unchanged when `.pre-commit-config.yaml` exists
- `-p` flag accepts both YAML and TOML files
- No new dependencies

## Summary by Sourcery

Add support for syncing pre-commit hook versions from uv.lock when using prek.toml configuration files, alongside existing .pre-commit-config.yaml support.

New Features:
- Support syncing hook versions in prek.toml configs using a new TOML-aware processor.
- Allow the CLI to auto-detect either .pre-commit-config.yaml or prek.toml when no config path is provided and to accept prek.toml explicitly via the -p flag.

Enhancements:
- Update the pre-commit hook metadata to trigger on changes to prek.toml as well as the existing config files.
- Adjust CLI error handling and config resolution so missing configuration files produce a consistent custom exit code.

Tests:
- Add unit tests for TOML processing logic covering mappings, quotes, line endings, and no-op scenarios.
- Add CLI integration tests for prek.toml covering auto-detection, explicit paths, write and diff modes, YAML precedence, and missing-config behavior.
- Update an existing CLI test to reflect the new exit code when the specified config file does not exist.

author: taearls
body:
## Summary

- Adds `get_spectrum` Tauri command returning the latest `SpectralSnapshot` as JSON for real-time frontend visualization polling
- Adds `timestamp_ms` field to `SpectralSnapshot` struct (milliseconds since Unix epoch)
- Adds `Engine::latest_snapshot()` method that drains all pending snapshots and returns only the most recent, preventing stale data accumulation
- Adds TypeScript `SpectralPeak` and `SpectralSnapshot` interfaces plus `getSpectrum()` async wrapper
- Returns `null` gracefully when engine is not running or no data is available yet
- Updates ROADMAP.md to mark #15 as completed

### Design decisions

- **Drain-to-latest pattern**: `latest_snapshot()` drains all buffered snapshots and returns only the freshest one, so the frontend always gets current data regardless of poll rate
- **Non-blocking throughout**: The audio processing thread uses `try_send` (bounded channel, capacity 4), and the Tauri command uses `try_recv` — neither side ever blocks
- **Mutex held briefly**: The `get_spectrum` command acquires the `AppState` mutex only long enough to call the non-blocking drain loop, so lock contention is minimal even at 60fps polling

Closes #15

author: airhorns
body:
Switch shard leases from keepalive-based (auto-expiring) to permanent
(persist until explicitly released). This ensures that if a node crashes,
its shards remain owned so the WAL can be recovered when it restarts,
preventing data loss from another node taking over without processing
the crashed node's unflushed writes.

Key changes:
- Etcd: Replace Lock API with KV transactions (put-if-absent/delete-if-owner)
- K8s: Remove lease renewal loop, remove expiry-based takeover
- Add startup lease reclamation (reclaim_and_open_shards) for both backends
- Add force_release_shard_lease as operator escape hatch for lost nodes
- Add ForceReleaseShard gRPC endpoint and siloctl command
- Update Alloy spec: remove leaseExpire, add forceReleaseLease, add
  flapPreservesLeases invariant (SILO-COORD-INV-14)
- Remove liveness_lease_id from etcd coordinator (only membership lease needed)

Test coverage for both etcd and k8s backends:
- Crash does not release shard lease
- Permanent lease blocks other nodes from acquiring
- Force-release allows reacquisition
- Graceful shutdown still releases leases
- Crash-restart reclaims and opens shards automatically
- Hash ring divergence on restart (reclaim then reconcile)
- Coordinator-level crash/force-release integration
- Different node_id does not reclaim another node's leases
- Force-release of non-existent shard returns ShardNotFound
- ForceReleaseShard gRPC endpoint (success + invalid ID error)

body:
## Summary
Improve Erdős #635 (non-divisibility condition on differences) by converting axioms to proved theorems and fixing an incorrect axiom.

## Progress
- **PROVED** `oddSet_admissible`: The set of odd numbers in {1,...,N} satisfies the 1-non-divisibility condition (via even/odd parity argument)
- **PROVED** `no_far_doubles`: In any t-admissible set, no element can be double of another at distance >= t
- **FIXED** `no_far_multiples`: Original axiom was mathematically incorrect for k >= 3. Renamed to `no_far_doubles` (k=2 only)

## Bug Fix
The original `no_far_multiples` axiom claimed `b ≠ k*a` for all k >= 2 in admissible sets. This is wrong:
- For k=3, a=5: `b-a = 2a = 10`, and `10 ∤ 15`, so the condition is NOT violated
- The divisibility `(k-1)a | ka` only holds when `(k-1) | k`, i.e., k = 2
- Fixed to `no_far_doubles` which correctly handles only the k=2 case

## Findings
- Problem reportedly resolved by ChatGPT-5.2/Tao via Elliott (1979)
- Key insight: difference of two odds is even; even numbers can't divide odd numbers
- `oddSet_card` converted to sorry (submittable to Aristotle)

## Status
**Outcome**: progress (2 axioms proved, 1 bug fixed)
**Docker Build**: Not verified (Docker overloaded)

body:
This pull request introduces several important improvements and additions to the codebase, focusing on enhancing theming, image handling, and button components, as well as updating dependencies and permissions for better Android support. The changes modernise the project's Compose setup, add new UI building blocks, and improve cross-platform theming support.

**Theming and UI Foundation:**
- Added an Android-specific implementation of `BookmarkTheme` to support dynamic colour schemes, system dark theme detection, and status bar customisation (`BookmarkTheme.android.kt`, `ShouldUseDarkTheme.android.kt`).
- Updated the main `App` composable to use the new `BookmarkTheme` instead of `MaterialTheme` for consistent theming across platforms (`App.kt`).

**Image Handling Enhancements:**
- Introduced a new `BookmarkImage` composable, supporting both URL and resource images with placeholder, error handling, and loading callbacks, using Coil for image loading (`BookmarkImage.kt`, `ImageConfiguration.kt`, `ImageExtensions.kt`).
- Added Coil dependencies for Compose and Ktor to enable image loading in Compose UI (`build.gradle.kts`).

**Button Components:**
- Added a comprehensive `BookmarkButton` composable supporting multiple styles, loading state, and accessibility roles, along with a preview and style enumeration (`BookmarkButton.kt`).
- Introduced `BookmarkEndTextButton` for end-aligned text buttons within rows (`BookmarkEndTextButton.kt`).

**Dependency and Build Improvements:**
- Refactored dependency declarations in `build.gradle.kts` to use the `libs.jetbrains.compose` catalogue for consistency and maintainability; added missing dependencies for Android and JVM targets.

**Android Permissions:**
- Added the `INTERNET` permission to the Android manifest to support network operations, such as image loading from URLs (`AndroidManifest.xml`).

**Other Utility Additions:**
- Added utility extensions for working with booleans (`BooleanExtensions.kt`) and type aliases for composable parameters and status bar side effects (`ComposableParam.kt`, `StatusBarSideEffect.kt`).

author: willibrandon
body:
## Summary

Resizing the terminal window caused a visible blank frame before the new content rendered. This happened because `OnResize()` immediately called `Renderer.Erase()`, which flushed a screen-clear to the terminal — creating a gap between the erase and the next render.

This PR fixes the flicker with two changes:

- **Synchronized output (DEC Mode 2026):** All render, erase, and clear operations are now wrapped in `\x1b[?2026h`/`\x1b[?2026l` markers. The terminal buffers everything between the markers and paints it as a single atomic frame. Terminals that don't support Mode 2026 silently ignore the sequences — no feature detection needed.

- **Deferred erase on resize:** `OnResize()` no longer calls `Erase()`. Instead it calls `ResetForResize()`, which resets renderer state (cursor position, last screen, style caches) without writing anything to the terminal. The actual erase happens inside the next render cycle, which is already wrapped in a sync block.

## What changed

**IOutput interface** — new `BeginSynchronizedOutput()` / `EndSynchronizedOutput()` methods across all 6 implementations:
- `Vt100Output`: real implementation — sets a flag, `Flush()` wraps buffer in Mode 2026 markers
- `Win32Output`, `PlainTextOutput`, `DummyOutput`: no-ops
- `Windows10Output`, `ConEmuOutput`: delegate to their internal `_vt100Output`

**Renderer** — three methods wrapped in begin/end with try/finally:
- `Render()`: sync block around screen diff + flush
- `Erase()`: sync block around erase sequence + flush
- `Clear()`: inlined erase logic (avoids nested sync blocks) + sync block

**Renderer.ResetForResize()** — new method that resets 9 state fields to initial values with zero terminal I/O

**Renderer.Diff** — full-redraw path uses `\x1b[H` (absolute cursor home) instead of relative `MoveCursor()`, which is safer after a resize when cursor position may be stale

**Application.RunAsync** — `OnResize()` calls `ResetForResize()` + `Invalidate()` instead of `Erase()`

## Tests

22 new tests in 2 files:

- `Vt100OutputSynchronizedOutputTests` (15 tests) — flag behavior, idempotency, marker ordering, overhead measurement, multi-write batching, flag lifecycle across flush cycles, exception safety, concurrent access
- `RendererSynchronizedOutputTests` (8 tests, rebased to 10) — render/erase/clear wrapping, no marker nesting in Clear, ResetForResize zero-IO and state reset, absolute cursor positioning on full redraw, DummyOutput and PlainTextOutput graceful degradation

Full regression: 9,333 tests pass, 0 failures.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — zero errors, zero warnings
- [x] `dotnet test` — 9,333 passed, 0 failed
- [x] `dotnet test --filter SynchronizedOutput` — all 22 new tests pass
- [x] TUI driver: resize get-input, fancy-zsh-prompt, calculator at multiple sizes — no blank frames

author: lex00
body:
Fixes #48703
Related to #38109, #13176

## Problem

The git panel can show stale branch and file status after switching back from a terminal where you ran git commands (checkout, rebase, reset, stash pop). Same thing happens after laptop sleep/wake.

Git state only refreshes when Zed sees changes inside `.git/` via filesystem events. If those events are lost, stale state persists indefinitely. No manual refresh, no periodic rescan.

## Approach

This is a safety net, not a targeted fix for a specific event-loss path. We can't reliably prove which FSEvents get dropped during sleep/wake or heavy IO, but we can make sure the git panel recovers when the user comes back to Zed.

Add `reload_repositories()` to GitStore, called from `Workspace::on_window_activation_changed` when the window becomes active. This triggers `schedule_scan()` for all repositories, running a full `git status .` on a background thread.

### Performance

`schedule_scan` uses keyed job deduplication (`GitJobKey::ReloadGitState`), so rapid window switches collapse into one scan. In large monorepos `git status` can be slow (see #43861). If this turns out to be a problem, a cooldown or debounce could be added, but the dedup already prevents the worst case.

## Changes

3 files, ~20 lines of production code:
- `git_store.rs`: new `reload_repositories()` method
- `workspace.rs`: call it on window activation
- `git_panel.rs`: test

## Test plan

- New: `test_git_panel_updates_on_reload_repositories` sets up git panel, changes git status without firing events (simulating lost FSEvents), calls `reload_repositories`, verifies panel updates
- All 12 existing git panel tests pass
- clippy clean

Release Notes:

- Fixed an issue where the git panel could show stale branch and file status after switching back from a terminal or after sleep/wake.

body:
This pull request updates how FFmpeg and FFprobe are sourced, located, and invoked in both the backend and the build scripts to ensure GPU encoder support and improved reliability across platforms. The main improvements are the use of bundled FFmpeg/FFprobe binaries (with GPU encoder support) by default, robust fallback to system binaries, and enhanced extraction logic for Windows builds.

**Backend: FFmpeg/FFprobe Path Management and Usage**
- Introduced `get_ffmpeg_path()` and `get_ffprobe_path()` utility functions in `app/data_paths.py` to consistently locate the correct FFmpeg/FFprobe binaries, preferring bundled versions with GPU encoder support and falling back to system PATH if needed.
- Updated all FFmpeg/FFprobe invocations in `app/services/transcoding.py` to use the dynamically determined paths (`FFMPEG`, `FFPROBE`) instead of hardcoding `"ffmpeg"` and `"ffprobe"`. This affects all subprocess calls for transcoding, probing, and encoder detection. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cR19-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL62-R70) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL113-R121) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL371-R379) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL429-R437) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL450-R458) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL478-R486) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL516-R524) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL769-R777) [[10]](diffhunk://#diff-ee7415f478927485bf1f5d2b29620c06633be0a36130a819795bc4a946fec45cL1044-R1052)
- Added logging to display which FFmpeg/FFprobe binaries are being used at runtime, aiding debugging and transparency.

**Build Script: FFmpeg/FFprobe Bundling**
- Changed Linux and Windows FFmpeg sources in `scripts/download-ffmpeg.cjs` to use builds with GPU encoder support (`BtbN` for Linux, "full" build for Windows).
- Enhanced Windows extraction logic to handle `.7z` archives using 7-Zip, PowerShell, or fallback methods, improving reliability for Windows builds.
- Ensured that extracted binaries are consistently located and moved to the correct location for bundling.

**Transcoding Improvements**
- Adjusted audio mapping in the video stacking function to map only the first audio stream from the first input, improving correctness for multi-audio-stream files.

These changes collectively ensure that the backend always uses a version of FFmpeg/FFprobe with GPU encoder support when available, and that the build process robustly provides these binaries across all supported platforms.
